newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT '96 profit up, sees further rise.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT '96 profit up, sees further rise.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) on Tuesday posted 1996 net profits up over nine percent to 2.46 billion guilders ($1.3 billion) and said it saw further profit growth in 1997.
Net profit per share in 1996 increased to 5.29 guilders from 4.89 in 1995, with the company raising its dividend to 2.85 guilders per ordinary share from 2.60.
"For 1997, KPN expects a substantial growth of turnover and a clear growth of the profit after taxes," the company said in a statement.
It added that it expected to double turnover from postal activities, partly as a result of the takeover of Australian express delivery service TNT.

The 1996 figures were right on expectations and most analysts were sticking to current forecasts, though on the Amsterdam exchange the shares were immediately marked down in a bout of profit taking after a steep rise yesterday.
The shares were trading down 0.90 guilders at 69.30 at 1430 GMT, after standing as high as 72.00 guilders before the results.
"The figures and forecast are in line with expectations and the dividend of 2.85 guilders per share was just below our estimate," said NIBStrating Securities analyst Rene Verhoef.
"The dip in the share price after the figures is overdone, since the stock was up before (the announcement) and the profits and outlook did not disappoint."

KPN said it based its expectations for future profit increases on strong growth of the market for mobile telecommunications and a continuing growth of demand for newly introduced and existing services.
But steady growth in sales would be accompanied by continuing pressure on prices, it added.
Investments in acquisitions and fixed assets mushroomed 78 percent to 8.72 billion guilders in 1996, the group said.

This was due both to high profile buys such as the takeover of Australia's TNT by PTT Post and the acquisition of key minority shareholdings in Telecom Eireann of Ireland and PT Telkomsel of Indonesia.
"Our (profit) expectation does not take into account the possible effects on the profit after taxes of further acquisitions or divestments in 1997," KPN said.
New takeovers were possible in the current year and KPN said it was keeping open the option of raising additional funds on the capital market in the course of 1997.
Analysts said the company might start to feel the force of competitive pressure in the increasingly deregulated telecommunications market during the current year.

"KPN forecasts more growth for 1997 which is good, but it would be interesting to hear how they intend to boost sales...as competition will become harder as new competitors enter the (Dutch) market," said Steven Vrolijk of ING Barings.
The company said its postal activities boosted turnover by 10 percent in 1996, due mainly to acquisitions, and analysts remained satisfied with performance in the sector.

"Postal activities seem to have done very well. Efficiency has increased, the hike in mail tariffs may have helped to lift income...Overall a nice increase in gross margin to some 14 percent at postal activities," said Joost van Beek, analyst at Van Meer James Capel.
